Answer: F
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates dextrocardia (heart on the right) and a gastric bubble on the right, confirming situs inversus totalis. In Kartagener's syndrome with situs inversus, the anatomical mirroring means that bronchiectasis, which typically affects the lower lobes, will appear more pronounced on the patient's morphological left lung (which is located on the viewer's right side), matching the extensive markings seen in the left hemithorax of this image.
